messages:
Maria C.: heads up — during the strict structured-output validator canary (v1.4) we’re seeing ~4.8% of live tool runs flagged as validation_failed and automatically routed to the fallback route.
Sam R.: ugh that’s higher than expected. do we have an example payload?
Maria C.: yeah, snippet from logs: ```{
  "request_id": "r_abc123",
  "tool_response": "{\"items\": [1,2,3], \"meta\": null}",
  "validation_error": "expected object for 'result' but got string"
}```
Kevin P.: is the fallback route identical model-wise? customers reported doubled token usage for some calls.
Maria C.: current policy: on validation_failed -> route to fallback_small (cheaper model) but we also log+re-run which increments usage for both attempts. causing double-counts in billing metrics.
Eva L.: that seems wrong for UX. two ideas: (1) soft-fail flag that returns structured warning and still deliver primary response without re-run, or (2) perform a silent repair attempt without billing the second run.
Sam R.: technical constraints: silent repair still executes model, so it counts tokens. we could change routing to return a structured error to the SDK and surface a client-side retry opt-in.
Kevin P.: product prefers no silent surprises — customers should see a single attempt or a clear fallback. how does this show up on dashboards?
Maria C.: dashboard currently shows per-route token usage and a counter for fallback invocations. but validation failures are not a separate metric so support teams see a spike in fallback usage and assume capacity issues.
Sam R.: proposal: add validation.{version}.reject_rate gauge and a validation.failure_tag dimension (reason enum). sample at 100% for canary, 10% for prod. send trace/span with tag validation.strict=true/false.
Eva L.: +1 on reason enums, we can map to quick UX messages: malformed-shape, missing-field, type-mismatch. that will make support triage easier.
Maria C.: also need a change to quota accounting: if validation failed and we short-circuit (no re-run), do not increment model token usage metric. patch idea: set header `X-Validation-Outcome: soft-warning` and the billing pipeline ignores second attempt when header present.
Sam R.: ok but billing pipeline lives in another service — need cross-team sync. I can draft a minimal contract: `validation_outcome` header values = [ok, soft-warning, hard-fail, routed]. and a short backfill rule for recent canary.
Kevin P.: schedule sync with billing + support. also update console messaging: when user clicks an invocation with validation tag show: "Output schema warning — trimmed/converted to best-effort" with link to docs.
Eva L.: rollout plan: 1) enable extra metrics (no behavior change), 2) surface warnings in console, 3) flip routing policy to soft-warning for 1% of traffic, 4) expand to 10% after 48h, 5) stop re-run -> change quota handling once billing team confirms.
Maria C.: can we also add sampling of raw failure payloads to s3 with pii scrub? we need small samples for debug.
Sam R.: yes — add `validation.sample_rate` per-reason; default 0.02 for prod, 1.0 for canary. include hashed user_id.
Maria C.: quick commands I used: `aws s3 ls s3://redwood-logs/validation-v1/ | tail -n 50` and `rg validation_failed -n logs/canary-2026-03-21.log`
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for validator v1.4 on eng-platform (slice: beta-users). :rocket:
Maria C.: I pushed a tiny non-behavioral PR to emit the reason enum and header: https://git.internal/r/redwood/validator/pulls/432
Kevin P.: remind me to update the changelog and add a short blurb in the console help center.
Eva L.: after billing sync we should add a console toggle: "Treat validation failures as warnings" so enterprise admins can opt-in.
Sam R.: noted. I’ll open an RFC with the header contract + sampling schema.
Maria C.: thanks everyone — monitoring alert for validation.reject_rate > 1% during canary. if we hit 3% we'll pause and roll back.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused automatically (validation.reject_rate = 3.7%). reference: alert#val-987.
Maria C.: rolling back v1.4 and creating a patch to lower strictness thresholds. will re-run the canary once patched.
Kevin P.: good call. file a postmortem note with timeline and customer-impact estimate if any.
Eva L.: adding owners: Maria (validator), Sam (telemetry + infra), Kevin (product messaging), Billing team (accounting).
Maria C.: noted — will send calendar invites and follow-ups. thanks :heart:
